author = "Deshe, Noa and Eliezer, Yifat and Hoch, Lihi and Itskovits, Eyal

abstract = "The notion that associative memories may be transmitted across
generations is intriguing, yet controversial. Here, we trained C.
elegans nematodes to associate an odorant with stressful
starvation conditions, and surprisingly, this associative memory
was evident two generations down of the trained animals. The
inherited memory endowed the progeny with a fitness advantage, as
memory reactivation induced rapid protective stress responses
that allowed the animals to prepare in advance for an impending
adversity. Sperm, but not oocytes, transmitted the associative
memory, and the inheritance required H3K9 and H3K36 methylations,
the small RNA-binding Argonaute NRDE-3, and intact neuropeptide
secretion. Remarkably, activation of a single chemosensory neuron
sufficed to induce a serotonin-mediated systemic stress response
in both the parental trained generation and in its progeny. These
findings challenge long-held concepts by establishing that
associative memories may indeed be transferred across
generations. \#\#\# Competing Interest Statement The authors have
declared no competing interest.",
